projects.name: Design and Extension of a Unity-Based Visual Authoring Tool for Bullet-Hell Games

sections.Abstract: Developing bullet-hell shoot ’em up (STG) games through separate scripts and interfaces complicates the coordination of bullet patterns, enemy movement, encounter timing, and boss behaviors. It also proposes constrained bullet-pattern variation for designer-controlled exploration of alternative attacks. This study aims to provide a unified visual authoring framework and a foundation for future algorithm-assisted STG content generation.
sections.Problem Statement:
Fragmented configuration complicates the coordination of enemy movement, bullet patterns, and encounter timing.
Repeated manual adjustments can make exploring alternative bullet patterns time-consuming.
The editor’s impact on authoring efficiency and usability remains unverified.
sections.Methodology:
Stage 1: Literature Review & Research Design
Review visual authoring and procedural content generation studies to identify STG development requirements.
Adopt Design Science Research and define structured authoring tasks and usability questionnaires.
Stage 2: Tool Design & Development
Develop ONYX STG Editor in Unity using C#, integrating stage timelines, movement paths, bullet patterns, boss phases, and reusable libraries.
Implement constrained pattern variation and validate authored content through the Code 81 prototype.
Stage 3: Evaluation & Analysis
Record task completion time, configuration errors, and perceived usability during structured authoring tests.
Measure runtime performance and collect player feedback on selected encounters to identify limitations and guide refinement.
sections.Implementation: This study implements ONYX STG Editor as a Unity-based visual authoring tool using C# and the EditorWindow framework. The tool integrates player configuration, enemy movement paths, stage timelines, projectile patterns, and multi-phase boss management within a coordinated interface. ScriptableObject assets and prefabs store reusable configurations, separating content authoring from runtime execution. Editor-based previews support content inspection, while frame-based scheduling and event conditions coordinate enemy spawning, attacks, and phase transitions. This study integrates the authored content into Code 81, a playable prototype containing a tutorial, a main stage, and a boss encounter. The prototype provides a practical environment for checking configuration behaviour and refining gameplay through iterative testing.
sections.Result: This study has produced a functional Unity-based visual authoring tool and a playable Code 81 prototype. Enemy formations, movement paths, projectile patterns, and boss phases can be configured, previewed, saved, and executed through reusable assets. The tutorial, main stage, and multi-phase boss encounter demonstrate the integration between editor configurations and runtime gameplay. Iterative testing has supported refinements to phase transitions, animation scaling, interface alignment, and gameplay feedback. These outcomes establish the technical feasibility of the integrated authoring workflow. However, improvements in authoring efficiency and perceived usability have not yet been established through formal user evaluation. Structured testing is therefore required before drawing conclusions about the tool’s effectiveness.
sections.Conclusion:
Contribution
Developed the ONYX STG Editor, integrating stage scheduling, enemy movement, bullet patterns, and boss phases within Unity.
Supported reusable content assets and editor-based previews, with gameplay integration through the Code 81 prototype.
Limitation
Limited to Unity-based 2D vertical-scrolling bullet-hell games.
Improvements in authoring efficiency and usability remain unverified.
Future Work
Conduct structured user evaluations of completion time, configuration errors, and usability.
Further develop and evaluate designer-controlled bullet-pattern variation.
sections.Game Objective:
To design and develop ONYX STG Editor for configuring enemy movement, projectile patterns, stage timelines, and boss behaviours, with Code 81 serving as the validation prototype.
To implement constrained bullet-pattern variation that generates alternative configurations within designer-defined limits while retaining manual editing control.
To evaluate the tool’s authoring efficiency and usability through task completion time, configuration errors, and user feedback.

projects.author: Tang Feilian

projects.name: Investigating The Impact Of Fourth Wall Breaks (FWB) In Player’s Fear And Immersion Level In Horror Games

sections.Abstract: This study investigates how Fourth Wall Breaks (FWB) impact player fear and immersion in horror games. A custom first-person horror prototype, “Twich”, developed in Unity Engine, 35 participants were tested using STAI-6, PANAS-SF, and IEQ-SF. Results demonstrated that FWB events significantly heighten player’s fear level (p < 0.05). However, heightened fear level correlates weakly with player immersion (r = 0.249), suggesting that although FWB effectively intensifies horror, its relationship with overall player immersion is complex and relies on broader game design factors.
sections.Problem Statement:
Lack of empirical evidence regarding the impact of FWB on player fear levels.
Relationship between FWB-induced fear emotions and player immersion remains underexplored.
FWB is not widely utilized in AAA companies.
sections.Methodology:
Stage 1: Literature Review & Research Design
Conduct a comprehensive literature review to identify FWB’s key design strategies and implementations. 
Construct research design elements including sampling method and questionnaire design.

Stage 2: Prototype Design & Development
Develop a custom PC horror prototype using Unity game engine, adopting Ramadan & Widyani’s (2013) Game Development Life Cycle (GDLC).

Stage 3: Research Evaluation & Analysis
Data collection was conducted through a 30-45 minutes playtest, using pre-test/post-test method.
Paired t-test and Pearson correlation was conducted to evaluate design effectiveness.
sections.Implementation:
Initiation
Establishes and defines the game concept and gathers relevant game references (Parasocial, DDLC!).

Pre-production
Focuses on core game designs, including the storyline, game mechanics, and FWB methods. 
Translated into Game Design Document (GDD).

Production
Translates the game design into a playable prototype using Unity engine.
Integrates core system such as player movement, mini puzzles, interaction system, and storyline system.
Implements three FWB methods (Medium Manipulation, Outside Medium Play, Player Prominent Involvement) without violating the device’s data.

Testing
Iterative testing is conducted to identify and resolve bugs, ensuring the game and the FWB events function as intended. 

Release
The finalized prototype is deployed under a controlled playtesting session to collect participants data.
sections.Result:
RQ1 ✔ H1 ✔
Participants’ fear level significantly increases (p < .001) after the gameplay.
Player Prominent Involvement yields the highest level of fear.

RQ2 ✘ H2 ✘
Weak positive correlation between the average fear level increase (ΔSTAI-6) and total immersion scores (IEQ-SF), suggested that FWB is not the sole factor that impacts player immersion. (r = 0.249, p = 0.149).

Most Enjoyable Game Design Element
27 out of 35 participants agree they enjoy Fourth Wall Breaks (FWB) events the most.
Most participants report that FWB events successfully increase their level of fear and uneasiness based on qualitative feedbacks.
sections.Conclusion:
Contributions
Provided empirical evidence on the impact of FWB in horror games.
Exposed the potential of FWB in invoking genuine fear in horror games genre.
Proposed 3 types of FWB implementation.

Limitations
Small and limited sample size (35 participants).
Relied on subjective self-report measures, which may not effectively capture participants’ fear level fluctuations.

Future Work
Incorporate physiological measuring equipment, such as heart rate monitors and galvanic skin response sensors.
Expand research to investigate the specific impact of FWB on player engagement.
sections.Game Objective:
1. To design and develop a horror game prototype that implements Fourth Wall Break methods.
2. To quantitatively evaluate the impact of Fourth Wall Break on player fear and anxiety using the PANAS-SF and STAI-6 psychometric scales.
3. To assess how players fear and anxiety responses towards Fourth Wall Break are associated with their immersion level using IEQ-SF.

projects.author: Bryan Law Ee Jiun

projects.name: Quest of Two: A Collaborative AR Board Game to Foster Inclusive Social Interaction Between Autistic and Neurotypical  Children

sections.Abstract: Quest of Two is a multiplayer Augmented Reality (AR) board game designed to foster inclusive social interaction between autistic children and their peers. Combining a physical quest board with digital AR elements, the game requires players to collaborate through shared objectives and interdependent gameplay mechanics. The prototype was evaluated through a mixed-method study involving three children: one autistic, one neurotypical and one with ADHD. Findings suggest that AR can encourage physical co-presence and shared attention. However, meaningful social interaction also depends on the rapport between players and appropriate social support.
sections.Problem Statement:
- Screen dependency can reduce face-to-face interaction.
- Children may miss important social cues such as eye contact, gestures and body language.
- Digital games do not automatically encourage collaboration between players.
sections.Methodology:
A. Participants: 3 children aged 10–12
P1: Autistic participant (ASD)
P2: Neurotypical participant (NT)
P3: Participant with ADHD

B. Testing Procedure: Preliminary Trial → Structured Training → Formal Experiments
Experiment 1: P1 + P2 (Sibling / High Rapport)
Experiment 2: P1 + P3 (Cousin / Lower Rapport)

C. Data Collection
Modified System Usability Scale (SUS)
Fun-Difficulty Sorter
Video Observation Logs
Semi-Structured Interviews

*Video observations and interviews were jointly analysed and validated by the researcher and a certified ABA shadow aide.
sections.Result:
Experiment 1: P1 + P2 (Sibling)
Interaction developed from parallel play into collaboration.
P1 spontaneously taught P2 how to scan the cards.
P1 adjusted the board to help P2 see the game better.
P1 demonstrated a mentor-like role.

Experiment 2: P1 + P3 (Cousin)
Cooperation became more transactional.
Verbal coordination was difficult for P3.
P3 reported not feeling closer to the partner.
Additional support was needed to facilitate interaction.

Insight: Cooperation does not necessarily mean social connection.
sections.Conclusion:
Contribution
Developed a collaborative AR board game that encourages physical interaction and shared attention.
Demonstrated the Mentor Effect, where the autistic participant guided his neurotypical peer.

Limitation
Small sample size (3 participants).
Pre-existing relationships between participants.
Short-term testing duration.

Future Work
Expand participant numbers and diversity.
Test with unfamiliar player pairs.
Conduct longitudinal studies.
Introduce multisensory gameplay elements.
sections.Game Objective:
1. To investigate how traditional screen-based games can limit face-to-face social interaction among autistic children and their peers.
2. To design and develop a collaborative multiplayer AR board game using a Neurodiversity-Oriented Design approach.
3. To assess the prototype's usability and investigate its potential to encourage inclusive social interaction through user testing.

projects.author: Tan Hao

projects.name: The Effect Of Adventure Game on Intrinsic Motivation in Learning Inorganic Chemistry: A Study on The Topic of Salt

sections.Abstract: Learning the salts topic in chemistry can be challenging because of its abstract concepts. This study developed Flame Warden, a 3D adventure educational game, and evaluated changes in learners’ intrinsic motivation. Guided by Self-Determination Theory, the game integrates chemistry learning with storytelling, exploration, and puzzles. A one-group pre-test/post-test study involved 43 participants aged 19–25 who were not studying or working in chemistry-related fields. Results showed significant improvements in interest/enjoyment, autonomy, competence, and relatedness (all p < .001). Puzzle-solving and the Light Station were perceived as particularly motivating, suggesting the potential of adventure games to support motivation in chemistry learning.
sections.Problem Statement:
The salts topic involves abstract concepts that can be difficult to understand through rote memorization.
Research on game-based learning for the salts topic remains limited, particularly for adventure games.
Empirical evidence on the relationship between adventure games and intrinsic motivation in chemistry learning is scarce.
sections.Methodology:
The research comprised three stages:
Literature Review and Research Design: Identify suitable adventure game elements and establish a quantitative, one-group pre-test/post-test design.
Prototype Development: Develop the game using an adapted Game Development Life Cycle, including initiation, preproduction, production, testing and expert validation, pilot testing with five participants, and deployment.
Evaluation and Analysis: Recruit 43 non-chemistry participants aged 19–25. Participants completed a pre-test, played the game for approximately 30–40 minutes, and completed a post-test.

An adapted Intrinsic Motivation Inventory used a five-point Likert scale to assess interest/enjoyment, autonomy, competence, and relatedness. Data were analyzed using reliability analysis, descriptive statistics, paired-samples t-tests, and Cohen’s d in Microsoft Excel and jamovi.
sections.Implementation:
Flame Warden is a 3D PC adventure educational game developed using Unity and C#, focusing on the flame colours produced by different metal salts. Players become a trainee Flame Warden exploring Crystfire Hollow to recover a stolen flame and reactivate its tower. Chemistry content is embedded in exploration, puzzle-solving, and battles.

Key features include:
Story and exploration: Cutscenes, unlockable areas, NPC interactions, and dialogue choices.
Chemistry puzzles: Match flame colours, burn ore candles, arrange notes, and activate the tower.
Light Station: Process ores and solutions into fragments and burn them to produce coloured flames.
Supporting systems: Item collection, inventory, HP, and turn-based battles

The design applies Self-Determination Theory through player choices, progressive challenges and feedback, and character interactions. The prototype underwent internal testing, chemistry content validation, and pilot testing before evaluation.
sections.Result:
All four motivation subscales increased significantly after gameplay (n = 43; all p < .001).

SubscalePre-test meanPost-test meanCohen’s d

Subscale	Pre-test mean	Post-test mean	Cohen’s d
Interest/Enjoyment	2.42	4.45	1.67
Autonomy	2.44	4.28	1.43
Competence	2.67	4.56	1.67
Relatedness	2.73	4.47	1.4


The most motivating elements were the Drag & Burn Candle Puzzle (51.2%), Drag & Drop Note Puzzle (37.2%), and Light Station (32.6%). Storyline and cutscenes were the most popular feature (53.5%).

Perceived learning value averaged 4.60/5, and 100% of participants expressed willingness to play similar games covering other chemistry topics.
sections.Conclusion:
Contribution
Developed Flame Warden, a 3D adventure game for learning the salts topic.
Provided evidence of improved intrinsic motivation following gameplay.
Identified puzzles and resource management as promising motivational elements.
Limitations
No control group to establish a causal relationship.
Small sample of 43 participants outside chemistry-related fields.
Evaluation covered only short-term motivation and one chemistry topic; learning outcomes were not assessed.
Future Work
Include a control group and a larger sample of current chemistry students.
Assess knowledge acquisition, academic performance, and long-term motivation.
Extend the game to other chemistry topics.
sections.Game Objective:
Identify common adventure game elements suitable for game-based learning through a literature review.
Develop a 3D adventure educational game on the salts topic.
Evaluate changes in learners’ intrinsic motivation after playing the game.
Identify game elements perceived as enhancing learning motivation.

projects.author: Tan Xin Huey

projects.name: Exploration vs Goal-Driven Tasks: The Impact of Task Complexity on VR Cybersickness and Presence

sections.Abstract: This project explores how different gameplay tasks affect VR motion sickness (cybersickness) and the feeling of being inside a virtual world (presence). A medieval tavern VR game was developed using Unity, featuring free exploration and goal-driven challenges. A user study involving 42 participants compared their experiences. The findings offer insights into designing comfortable and engaging VR games.
sections.Problem Statement:
Cybersickness: VR can cause dizziness, nausea and other discomfort.
Presence: Different gameplay activities may influence how connected players feel to the virtual world.
Research Gap: Limited research directly compares free exploration and structured objectives in the same interactive indoor VR environment.
sections.Methodology:
Stage 1: Research & Design
Reviewed existing research on VR user experience.
Designed two task conditions within the same virtual environment.
Stage 2: VR Development
Developed a medieval tavern game using Unity and Meta Quest 3.
Implemented navigation, object interaction, and gameplay objectives.
Stage 3: User Testing
42 participants, divided into two groups of 21.
Each participant experienced one gameplay mode.
Collected SSQ (motion sickness) and IPQ (presence) questionnaire responses.
Stage 4: Analysis
Compared both groups to evaluate the effects of task complexity on VR experience.
sections.Implementation:
VR Game Development
Developed a two-floor medieval tavern using Unity and Meta XR SDK, featuring teleportation, object interaction, task tracking, and environmental storytelling.
Exploration Mode
Freely explore five areas and discover hidden stories.
Interact with objects without fixed puzzle objectives.
Goal-Driven Mode
Explore the tavern and collect three colored gems.
Arrange the gems in the correct order to unlock the exit.
sections.Result:
Player Feedback
Participants rated the gameplay, interactions tutorial and task instructions positively.
Insight
The findings highlight the importance of holistic VR game design, where task complexity, interaction, and movement systems work together to shape player comfort and immersion.
sections.Conclusion:
Contributions
Developed a playable VR game with two distinct task modes.
Found that goal-driven tasks did not significantly increase cybersickness or presence.
Limitations
Developed a playable VR game with two distinct task modes.
Found that goal-driven tasks did not significantly increase cybersickness or presence.
Future Work
Introduce more challenging puzzles and interactive features.
Test larger participant groups and collect movement data.
sections.Game Objective:
To review existing theories and empirical studies related to VR task complexity, cybersickness and presence.
To design and develop an indoor VR game prototype that includes both an exploration task and a goal-driven task.
To evaluate participants’ cybersickness and presence after experiencing the assigned VR task condition.

projects.author: Liu Yunyi

projects.name: Design and Evaluation of Gesture-Based Multi-Element Combat Interaction in a Mixed Reality RPG Prototype

sections.Abstract: Gesture-based combat in mixed reality requires players to select abilities, cast repeatedly, interpret feedback, and learn controls under pressure. This study designed and evaluated MR Elemental Combat, a Unity prototype using Meta XR/OVR hand tracking on Meta Quest 3. It separates element selection from casting and introduces Fire, Water, and Lightning through staged challenges, rewards, and multimodal feedback. Evaluation combined functional testing and a post-playtest questionnaire with 21 participants. All seven questionnaire dimensions scored above 4.30/5; overall satisfaction averaged 4.70/5. The findings support the feasibility and initial usability of the interaction design, while tutorial clarity, recognition reliability, and combat depth remain priorities.
sections.Problem Statement:
Repeated gesture input under combat pressure can lead to missed recognition, false triggers, and physical or cognitive burden.
Multi-element controls must communicate selection, casting, and progression without introducing too many gestures at once.
Gesture recognition alone does not establish whether an integrated MR combat experience is learnable, usable, and engaging.
sections.Methodology:
Stage 1: Design and Development
A formative design-and-evaluate approach guided iterative development in Unity and Meta XR/OVR. Gesture mappings, staged tutorials, and feedback were refined using the simulator and Quest 3.

Stage 2: Functional and User Testing
Core systems were checked against a 13-function checklist. A convenience sample of 21 adults completed gameplay tasks on Quest 3, a background questionnaire, post-playtest ratings, and optional written feedback.

Stage 3: Analysis
Five-point ratings were summarised using descriptive statistics across seven dimensions. Negatively worded items were reverse-coded before aggregation. Seven written responses were grouped into feedback themes.
sections.Implementation:
MR Elemental Combat | Unity / C# / Meta XR / Meta Quest 3

Select, then cast: predefined gestures choose Fire, Water, or Lightning; one palm-forward action casts the current element.
Learn through progression: five stages introduce targets, enemy encounters, mixed-element challenges, fragments, and tower-based unlocks before the final boss.
Unlock advanced actions: a thumbs-up gesture activates progression-gated abilities, including a fire stream and water shield.
Read the outcome: particles, audio, element indicators, health bars, and reward prompts communicate action results.
sections.Result:
All 13 functional checks passed in the reported test. Seven questionnaire dimension means ranged from 4.33 to 4.70/5 (n = 21).
Reward/unlock clarity scored 4.76 and progression-supported learning 4.71. Tutorial instructions scored 4.24; three of seven written comments concerned instruction/UI clarity.
These descriptive findings reflect initial user perceptions, not measured recognition accuracy or an advantage over controllers.
sections.Conclusion:
Contribution
Demonstrated a playable bare-hand MR combat loop combining element selection, shared casting, staged learning, and feedback.
Provided formative user evidence to guide further interaction design.
Limitations
Small convenience sample and short testing sessions.
Mainly self-report evidence; no detailed automatic performance logs or controlled input comparison.
Future Work
Add visual/bilingual tutorials and gesture calibration.
Log recognition failures and response times; expand combat depth and comparative testing.
sections.Game Objective:
1. Design gesture-based multi-element combat with clear action mapping, staged learning, and multimodal feedback.
2. Implement a playable Unity/Meta XR prototype integrating casting, enemies, rewards, progression, and boss combat.
3. Evaluate functionality and users' perceptions of learnability, usability, responsiveness, reliability, comfort, immersion, and satisfaction.

projects.author: Mi Yuhan

projects.name: Wonderland Arcane

sections.Game Concept:
The theme of this game was designed based on Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
The player will take on the role of Alice and embark on an adventure in a mysterious and perilous realm.
Pick up your magic wand, eliminate the enemies that stand in your way, and rescue the trapped queen!
sections.Storyline: The territory ruled by the queen was poorly controlled and, due to long-term neglect, had been invaded by many outsiders, causing chaos and unrest. The player's Alice needs to go through numerous dangerous situations to rescue the queen.
sections.Characters: Protagonist: Alice Antagonist: Mushroom, Dragon, Ghost, Goblin, Huge Monster
sections.Level Design:
Level 1: Basic button instruction, Basic enemies.
Level 2: Stronger enemies.
Level 3: Enemy Fortress — Hidden Map and challenging final boss.
sections.Game Mechanics:
Mechanic: The enemy will track the player.
When the player enters the detection range of the enemy, the enemy will start to track the player.

Mechanic: Collect resources.
During the game, players can collect resources that can be used to restore their health and magic power.

Mechanic: Teleportation point.
Each map has a teleportation point. When the player touches it, they will be teleported to the next map.

projects.author: Emily Lim Jia Qi, Jeffrey gan Beng Han, Khoo Jia Hui, Lim Gui Xuan, Li Xinzhuo

projects.name: The Most Amazing Adventure of Bartholomew

sections.Game Concept: The Most Amazing Adventure of Bartholomew is a 3-level fantasy FPS built around objective-based progression, fluid movement, and high-fantasy combat. Players step into the shoes of Bartholomew, a brave adventurer tasked with breaking a magical dragon curse that has ravaged the realm. To succeed, players must master dynamic combat, explore deceitful environments, and reclaim powerful relics to restore peace to a fallen kingdom.
sections.Storyline: Bartholomew’s journey begins in Old Ravenwood to uncover the lost lore of the village's tragedy. The path leads to the Sacred Cemetery’s to reveal the dark origins of the King's Curse, and final ascent of the corrupted Castle. There, Bartholomew must dethrone King Vargnir and claim his Crown to permanently break the dragon curse and save the realm.
sections.Characters:
Antagonist: 
Galgh - The Corrupted Guardian
Malazar - A Skeleton Necromancer
King Vagnir - Gilded Tyrant
sections.Level Design:
Level 1: Old Ravenwood
Environment: Overgrown ruins with mutated cactuses and corrupted mushrooms.
Boss Encounter: Gahlg, The Corrupted Guardian
Level 2: The Sacred Cemetery
Environment: Fog-drenched graveyard swarming with skeleton warriors and archers.
Boss Encounter: Malazar, a Skeleton Necromancer
Level 3: The Castle
Environment: Grand, corrupted halls guarded by royal knights and archers.
Boss Encounter: King Vargnir, The Gilded Tyrant
sections.Game Mechanics:
Dynamic Arsenal: Players start with a Bow and unlock the Militia Crossbow and Necromancer’s Staff, featuring unique mechanics like multi-enemy piercing projectiles.
Fluid Traversal: Built for vertical speed with rapid combat dashing, ladder climbing, and fall damage to enhance platforming stakes.
Impactful Combat: Physics-driven combat with heavy weapon knock-back, dynamic spawners, and NavMesh AI for unstoppable & persistent enemy tracking.
Survival Systems: Gathering resource drops and healing supplies scattered throughout levels sustain players in intense encounters.
Immersive Design: Includes interactive checkpoints, a full HUD UI, custom combat VFX, and tailored audio/BGM.

projects.author: Ellena Gazali, Liew Yok Han, Kenderson

projects.name: Alice: Unwound

sections.Game Concept: Alice: Unwound is a narrative-driven 3D action-adventure game inspired by Alice in Wonderland. Set in a surreal world where time and space are distorted, the game explores themes of fate, choice, and breaking free from an endless loop. As the story unfolds, players gradually uncover the hidden truth about this mysterious world, navigate unexpected challenges, and make final choices that shape Alice's destiny.
sections.Storyline: Alice explores and repairs broken clocks across a fractured world, discovers evidence of her past failures, then confronts Red Queen to end the loop.
sections.Characters: Protagonist: Alice, Antagonist: Red Queen, Narrator: Cheshire Cat
sections.Level Design:
Level 1: Forest & Clock Puzzle I — The Beginning of the Loop
Level 2: Reversed Town & Clock Puzzle II — Distorted Time
Level 3: Cemetery & Timed Parkour Chase — The Truth Revealed
Level 4: Red Queen’s Territory & Chessboard — Confront Red Queen
sections.Game Mechanics:
• Exploration & Collection: Explore the game world and collect props and weapons.
• Combat: Switch between three weapons—dual blades, a greatsword, and magic—to chain combos and dodge enemy attacks. Build up energy during combat to activate Phase 2, unleashing enhanced attacks and powerful abilities for each weapon.
• Parkour & Platforming: Jump, climb, vault, and use a grappling hook to overcome obstacles and traverse challenging environments.
• Puzzle: Rotate and connect clock components to restore broken clocks.
• Chess: Combine chess strategy with direct combat to defeat Red Queen and influence the ending.

projects.author: Bi Yuhan, Lin Daiyao, Lin Xinyu, Wang Ya, Wu Qianyi

projects.name: AstroRail

sections.Game Concept: AstroRail is a sci-fi endless runner where players control an astronaut navigating a futuristic space railway. Players dodge obstacles, collect stars, and choose branching paths while exploring rooftop areas through teleporters to battle robots and collect power-ups. The goal is to survive as long as possible and achieve the highest score.
sections.Characters:
Protagonist: Astronaut
Antagonist: Robot Enemies
sections.Level Design:
Astrorail is divided into two main gameplay environments：
1. Main Railway - The primary running area consists of three lanes, obstacles, collectibles, and branching paths. Players must react quickly to hazards and select directions at intersections.
2. Rooftop Area - An alternative area accessible through teleporters. Players encounter hostile robots, shoot enemies, collect keys and rewards, and use return teleporters to rejoin the main railway.
sections.Game Mechanics:
1. Auto Running: The astronaut runs forward automatically.
2. Movement: Switch lanes, jump, and slide to avoid obstacles.
3. Route Selection: Choose different paths at intersections.
4. Collectibles: Collect stars, keys, and power-ups.
5. Teleportation: Travel between railway and rooftop areas.
6. Combat: Shoot hostile robots in rooftop areas.
7. Endless Generation: New paths continuously generate as players progress.

projects.author: Chan Yikka

projects.name: Regalia: The Lost Grail

sections.Game Concept: Regalia: The Lost Grail is a 3rd Person 3D action-adventure game inspired by classic adventure games. Set in a mythical island where extreme environments are located, the game allow players to freely explore the vast environments and uncover the legends buried in the island.
sections.Characters:
Protagonist: John
Antagonist: Captain Marc, Monsters
sections.Level Design:
Level 1: Abandoned Island — Discover myths & gear up.
Level 2: Underwater Pirate Ship — Solve Puzzles & discover truths with swimming enemies.
Level 3: Underwater Shrine — Collection puzzle & mini-boss fight.
Level 4: Cave – Monster Chase scene & submit collected totems
Level 5: Abandoned Fortress – Final Boss Fight
sections.Game Mechanics:
1. Exploration: Players complete objectives, defeat or avoid monsters, and progress through levels while uncovering more of the game’s story.
2. Puzzles: A variety of puzzles to keep players engaged. 
3. Quick Time Events: Players must react quickly to these events to successfully unlock specific items or release themselves from detainment.
4. Swimming Movement: Two types of movements are incorporated. Normal movements and swimming movements to better stimulate the underwater scenes.
5. Monster Chase Scene: Monster chases the player and the player must act fast to find a path and escape from danger.
6. Challenging Boss Fights: Fight the final boss which contains 2 phases and a variety of attacks, challenging players to evade and attack at the right times.

projects.name: Whispers of Youzhu

sections.Game Concept: Whispers of Youzhu is a fantasy action-adventure game inspired by Chinese cultivation mythology. Players follow Ji Hua, a talented cultivator seeking to restore the declining Youzhu Sect. Through combat, exploration, and NPC interactions, players complete quests, battle monsters, and uncover hidden secrets. The journey leads to a final confrontation that reveals the truth behind their mission.
sections.Characters:
Protagonist: Ji Hua
Antagonist: Ah Qiang, Boss
sections.Level Design:
Plot
Ji Hua seeks to restore the declining Youzhu Sect by defeating a powerful demon, but discovers hidden truths along the journey.

Level Design
Level 1: Bamboo Sect — Basic combat, monster hunting, and elder quests.
Level 2: Western Village — NPC interactions, exploration, and clue gathering.
Level 3: Demon Forest — Enemy chases, environmental obstacles, final boss battle, and truth revelation.
sections.Game Mechanics:
Core Gameplay Mechanic: Quest-Driven Exploration & Combat, Players explore different areas, complete story quests, battle enemies, and uncover secrets to progress through the game.
1. Movement: Walking, running, jumping, wall climbing, and Qinggong.
2. Combat: Weapon-based attacks, enemy battles, and boss fights.
3. Exploration: Map navigation, teleportation, and environmental interactions.
4. Quest & NPC: Dialogue, missions, and story progression.
5. Inventory & Upgrades: Item collection, healing, weapon crafting, and upgrades.
6. Player Progression: Health, stamina, EXP, and respawn system.
7. UI & Audio: Minimap, menus, quest tracking, BGM, and sound effects.
8. Enemy AI: Enemy movement, attack patterns, health systems, and boss phases.

projects.name: We Were Mummies

sections.Game Concept: We Were Mummies is a two-player online co-op escape puzzle game set in an ancient Egyptian tomb. Two thieves cursed into mummies must communicate and work together to solve puzzles, escape, and defeat the guardian statue to break the curse.
sections.Storyline: Two greedy thieves sneak into an ancient Egyptian tomb to steal a sacred relic. When they open its coffin, the guardian statue curses them and turns them into mummies. Trapped underground, they must work together to escape and defeat the guardian to break the curse.
sections.Game Objective: Work together to solve cooperative puzzles, escape every chamber of the tomb, and defeat the guardian statue to break the curse and return to human form.
sections.Characters:
Protagonist – Thief 1 (Mummy): a cursed thief who becomes Blind in Level 2.
Protagonist – Thief 2 (Mummy): a cursed thief who becomes Deaf in Level 2.
Antagonist – Guardian Statue (Giant King): the tomb’s guardian who cursed the thieves, fought as the final boss.
sections.Level Design:
Level 1: Separated. Players solve the Gates of Colour maze and the Mirror Mimic pose puzzle from separate rooms.
Level 2: Blind & Deaf. Players guide each other through Dropping Tiles and Gaze of Bastet.
Final Level: Giant King. Players knock the boss into 8 pillars to break the curse.
sections.Game Mechanics:
Main mechanic: neither player can progress alone.
-Carry and place torches.
-Aim and throw objects.
-Interact with levers, buttons and pressure plates.
-Blind and Deaf curses in Level 2.
-In-game voice chat.
-Boss fight: hit the boss twice to knock him into the pillars.
sections.Development Process:
Concept: defined the game idea, puzzle rules and environment design.
Blockout: prototyped level layouts in ProBuilder.
Modelling: refined rooms and structures in Blender.
Environment: built the full levels in Unity using the Synty Polygon Ancient Egypt pack.
Mechanics: scripted player actions, puzzles and the boss in C# with reusable interfaces.
Multiplayer: added online co-op with Photon PUN 2 and custom voice chat.
Cutscenes: created story, hint and ending sequences with Unity Timeline.
Version control: used GitHub branches to merge the team’s work.
sections.Ideation & Inspiration: The game is inspired by the co-op puzzle game We Were Here, which is built around teamwork and communication. We chose an Ancient Civilization theme set in Egypt because its pyramids, hidden tombs, relics and legendary curses suit an escape puzzle adventure. It uses a stylized art style with vibrant colours and simplified characters.

projects.author: Angel Ling Zhi

projects.name: Traces of Warmth

sections.Game Concept: Traces of Warmth is the immersive opening level for the fantasy FPS The Most Amazing Adventure of Bartholomew. It is set in a recently deserted waterfront village where players navigate a dual-path layout through custom-built ruins and architecture. The rich environment features a sacred water altar, a rotating water wheel, and rustic village houses connected by wooden planks and stone steps. It provides a highly cohesive, atmospheric exploration experience for players.
sections.Development Process:
1. Concept & Spatial Mapping
Designed the game world blueprint through initial sketches and layout mapping to establish structural flow, pacing, and core gameplay zones.

2. Prototyping & Level Design
Translated blueprints into Unity using ProBuilder for greyboxing, establishing fundamental terrain blocks and navigation pathways

3. Asset Creation & Modeling
Modeled some custom 3D objects using ProBuilder such as modular village architecture, watchtower interiors, mechanical elements like the rotating water wheel, and feature props such as broken arches and ancient lanterns.

4. Visual Effects & Environment Integration
Implemented dynamic elements and shaders, such as incorporating custom water shaders, particle effects, and environmental detailing to bring the fantasy setting to life.

5. Post-Processing & Atmospheric Polish
Applied post-processing effects and color grading to unify the art style, enhance the visual mood, and maximize immersion for the player.

sections.Game Concept: “Bloom to Canvas” is a painting VR game designed for Meta Quest 3. It is a immersive painting simulator, where the player creates their paint from scratch, uses it in the creation of their masterpieces, and proudly displays it at the end (with a sudden earthquake occurring afterwards).

sections.Game Mechanics:
Material Creation and Learning Through Interaction
In the first level, the player collects four flowers of each primary color (red, blue, and yellow). These flowers are crushed and mixed with water to create paint.
VR Painting on Floating and 3D Surfaces
Players can paint in free space and on 3D surfaces using five different brushes and one eraser. 
Environmental Interaction and Physical Engagement
The player must physically retrieve the paintings and return them to their correct locations by climbing the tree inside and walking around.

Overall, the game demonstrates how VR painting can be integrated into a broader interactive narrative rather than functioning as an isolated creative tool.

D12 Movement & Risk Tiles: Roll a 12-sided die  to travel Low, Medium, and High-Risk hex tiles while managing economy resources.
Trivia-Powered Role Skills: Answer cybersecurity Trivia Cards to earn Knowledge Points, unlocking active skills on Roles like System Architect or Cunning Detective.
QR-Coded Phishing Traps: Scan physical QR Phishing Cards and deploy Malware to deceive teammates and sabotage their resources.

sections.Ideation & Inspiration:
A documentary about Chao Li Guan Mu, a traditional Chinese wooden coffin workshop in Muar, Johor, with nearly 99 years of history. projects.name: Everything EveryTrackAll at Once

sections.Storyline:
Beginning: 
Having lost her passion for music, Adult Xiaoye unexpectedly travels back to her childhood during a live performance.

Middle: 
She encounters her younger self and witnesses a painful conflict between the child and her mother over pursuing music.

Climax: 
Through a sound montage, Adult Xiaoye rediscovers her childhood self's pure love for music, leading to an emotional reconciliation with herself.

Ending: 
Reigniting her passion, Xiaoye returns to the present, where her adult and childhood selves perform together, symbolizing self-healing and rediscovered dreams.
sections.Characters:
1.Xiao Ye (Adult) 
Voice by: Wang Ya
2.Xiaohai (Child Xiaoye) 
Voice by: Lin Daiyao
3.Wang Tiemei 
Voice by:Li Wanning
sections.Ideation & Inspiration:
Inspired by Herstory, our project reimagines its themes of female empowerment and emotional healing through time travel, music, and mother-daughter relationships.

By combining sound montage with visual storytelling, we explore the rediscovery of childhood dreams and lost passion.

projects.name: Lost In Minecraft

sections.Storyline: The story follows a student who is immersed in playing Minecraft on her phone while walking around campus. Suddenly, a mysterious force pulls her into the game world. Excited by her unexpected adventure, she begins exploring around. However, her excitement turns into panic when Creepers attack her. As danger closes in, she discovers a mysterious portal and escapes back to the real world, only to realise that she is now a Minecraft character.
sections.Characters: 1. The Girl (Minecraft Veteran Player)
sections.Ideation & Inspiration: Our project is inspired by the idea of what would happen if someone suddenly entered the Minecraft world, we aim to create a fun and engaging story that connects fantasy with the real world.

projects.name: XMUM's Hero

sections.Storyline:
XMUM's hero, Jonathan does his routine check of the campus' perimeters when he suddenly noticed an enormous monster emerging from the campus lake. The monster starts to wreak havoc and destroys the campus bridge. 

Seeing this, Jonathon summons his transformation "Henshin" card and transforms into XMUM's hero while landing into the campus lake, facing off against the monster.
sections.Characters: 1. Jonathan (XMUM's Hero)
sections.Ideation & Inspiration: We are inspired by Hollywood movies such as Godzilla & Pacific Rim as well as childhood TV hero shows such as Kamen Rider and Ultraman. Hence, we wanted to produce a similar clip which revolves around a hero facing off against a monster.

projects.name: What's My Colour

sections.Storyline: A baby chameleon embarks on a magical journey to find his original colour, discovering along the way that his experiences and changing colours make him unique.
sections.Ideation & Inspiration: Inspired by the journey of self-discovery, our story explores the idea that we are shaped by every experience we encounter. Through a baby chameleon's search for its true colour, we hope to remind audiences that we are not defined by just one identity, but by all the colours that make us who we are.

projects.name: Kitty on the Way Home

sections.Storyline: Kitty, a spoiled house cat, accidentally ends up on a countryside farm, where three little chicks mistake her for their mother. Determined to return home, Kitty embarks on an unexpected adventure with the chicks, discovering the true meaning of friendship, courage, and family along the way.
sections.Ideation & Inspiration: Inspired by 101 Dalmatians, we wanted to create a heartwarming animal adventure that combines humor, friendship, and personal growth. Through Kitty's journey, we hope to highlight the importance of family, courage, and companionship.
